pr_title: Fix some bugs in the advanced scene import
pr_body:
Fix the following bugs:

- Start with the scene item selected, instead of showing an invalid view.
- Don't crash when selecting an unnamed material.
- Show `<Unnamed Material>` instead of no text for unnamed materials.

Fixes #54807
pr_comments: I recommend this pr be split into two prs. The unnamed material has problems, but the other bug is good.

issue_context.title: Crash when selecting empty/placeholder material in Advanced Import Settings dialog
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

4.0

### System information

Arch Linux

### Issue description

When importing a model (ex: cube.gltf), if exported with placeholder materials, when you import it in Godot, and click on the material, the whole engine crashes.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/42871796/140959095-d23b25bf-9a5c-42ba-8987-a27f27a9aded.png)


### Steps to reproduce

1. Open Blender and create cube
2. Export as glTF and under Geometry->Materials, select Placeholder
3. Import in Godot and double click the file
4. Open Materials tab or Meshes tab
5. Click on the material icon
6. Crash

### Minimal reproduction project

[MaterialCrash.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/7506192/MaterialCrash.zip)

The editor is crashing even if we use `Materials: Export` instead of `Materials: Placeholder` and the material is not linked to a valid shader within Blender.

review_comments:
@Calinou Reviews welcome.

I would use the classname of the p_material with deduplication.
I agree displaying a material ID somehow would be useful. I'd suggest using the form `[Unnamed Material 1234]`). Is there a prefereably deterministic material ID coming from the import system?

For what I understand from the import UI, the scene importer can provide a material ID.
But, if the ID is not provider, an autogenerated ID with a progressive number is created [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/59834/files#diff-26e1bde2ef7dbe454265bd0a7abc7fea36035cc84786acfd3bce9ee40edc8228R110).
I can display that (or a formatted version), but it's not deterministic.
Having a non deterministic name is worse than an empty string.

Different icons can be used here to distinguish whether the name is a deterministic material ID coming from the import system.

```
Ref<Texture2D> icon = get_theme_icon(material_data.has_import_id ? SNAME("StandardMaterial3D") : SNAME("ImportFail"), SNAME("EditorIcons"));
```
